messages:
nina: heads up — embeddings lane in eu-west is at ~95% GPU saturation and we're seeing a spike in 429s + TCP resets from the egress side. dashboards: https://dash.internal/r/redwood/emb-lane-eu-west :scream:
eng_oncall: joining. confirmed a sudden burst starting ~1769991100. top client is customer-zetta, ~4x normal qps. logs show repeated `connection reset by peer` from worker nodes. tail from router: `ERROR http: upstream reset during write`.
kai: rerank lane looks fine (20% use). embed lane queue depth is climbing — current in-flight ~980, backlog ~12k. admission control config (current):

```
admission:
  max_inflight: 1000
  per_customer_limit: 200
  small_req_threshold_ms: 50
  token_quota_per_min: 100000
```
lia: customer-zetta started a big reindex job overnight — batch size 512, concurrency 40. they hit the endpoint and aren't honoring client-side batching backoff. their payload shows 512 embeddings per request.
chris: immediate mitigation options:
- soft-429 per-customer when per_customer_limit exceeded (accept then requeue async)
- enable async spillover (requeue to embed-async SQS + worker pool)
- divert low-priority traffic to rerank lane (not ideal, different model)
I recommend soft-429 + async requeue for now so we don't OOM GPU queues. apply soft backpressure and prioritize tail-latency SLAs.
nina: agreed. let's toggle soft-429 and enable async spill for customer-zetta only. running the flag change now:

```
curl -X POST https://config.redwood/api/flags \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  -d '{"flag":"embed_soft_reject","target":"customer-zetta","value":true}'
```
deploy-bot: flag `embed_soft_reject` for customer-zetta -> true (revision 4821) :rocket:
eng_oncall: after flip, in-flight dropped to ~420 within 30s, queue depth decreasing. 429s now replacing hard connection resets. latency for small requests increased ~5ms due to requeue path.
kai: good short term. follow-ups:
- add token-based admission control (throttle by tokens/sec rather than reqs).
- schedule extra 4x GPU nodes in eu-west for next 12 hours (spot/on-demand tradeoff) — cost estimate ~ $1.2k/day. need finance sign-off for sustained expansion.
lia: can we also register a quantized model variant and route half of the non-critical requests to it? that'll reduce per-token GPU time.
chris: I'll create an incident ticket (INC-2026-301) and assign owners. immediate owners: eng_oncall -> stabilize, kai -> capacity/route changes, lia -> contact customer-zetta and ask to throttle ingestion.
eng_oncall: note — we're seeing ~2% of requests still hit `ECONNRESET` before soft-429 path kicks in. investigating connection pool retries on the router.
kai: config PR for token throttling exists (PR#716). it adds `token_rate_limit` and an admission hook that computes tokens = ceil(tokens_per_item * batch_size). routing rules can check `tokens_remaining` and either accept, soft-reject (requeue), or hard-reject.
lia: i'll reach out to customer-zetta now with suggested client changes: smaller batch sizes and exponential backoff. pinging @lia to sync on wording.
chris: created INC-2026-301 and linked dashboards + logs. filing follow-ups: COST-req for temporary GPU, PR#716 review, contact ticket for customer-zetta.
nina: summary action items:
- eng_oncall: monitor until queue < 20% and latency stable (owner)
- kai: expedite PR#716 review + prepare capacity pool (owner)
- lia: contact customer-zetta and request throttling (owner)
- chris: incident doc + cost request (owner)
thanks all :thumbsup: we can reopen if anything spikes again.
